quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before driving.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. You stop scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides. This makes you zone out and miss traffic that is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the other traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. Remember that cars entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They warn you about upcoming dangers. This sign tells you that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers.
Human error.
Bad weather.
Bad roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error.
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when they do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn.
All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road joins from the right side.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text and alert drivers to dangers ahead. This sign warns that the bridge may be too narrow to safely meet or pass a truck. Be careful and ready to slow down.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful behind them. When visibility is limited on a hill, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: A right turn
An intersection
A lane change
A road curve

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing bad drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to get through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you notice dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Keep going slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Stay on the right side of the road and keep going slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is using lights or sirens, move to the right side of the road as close as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies no matter which direction the emergency vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: When must children wear seat belts?

options.text: Anytime the car is moving
If their parents decide they should
If they want to
Only if they weigh less than 100 pounds

questions.correctAnswerText: Anytime the car is moving
questions.explanation: All children under 18 must wear a fastened seat belt anytime the car is moving on public roads. This applies no matter where they sit in the vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Before driving, always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat with an airbag.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up
Come to a complete stop
Turn on your headlights
Slow down and proceed carefully

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?

options.text: 55 mph
45 mph
30 mph
20 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive with extra care in these areas.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in construction zones?

options.text: They are reduced
They are doubled
They stay the same
There are no fines

questions.correctAnswerText: They are doubled
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines for traffic violations in construction zones are doubled. You may also face fines up to $1,000 and be required to complete a driving course.

questions.question: You are angry from something that happened at work. Before driving home, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you do not think about it
Drive fast on the highway to calm down
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving
Go to a bar and have drinks before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait to calm down before driving. Driving while emotionally upset is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and proceed carefully?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a car is following you too closely on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match the car behind you.
Move right to let the car pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let the driver pass and then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right to let the car pass.
questions.explanation: When a car follows you too closely on a multilane road, move right when it is safe. The left lane is for faster vehicles passing slower ones.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn to get attention. If the other car doesn't move, steer right. Don't steer left because the other driver might correct at the last second. Brake hard and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take your turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning left. You can enter the intersection if the light is green and no car ahead of you is turning left.

questions.question: When should drivers drive across or park on a median?

options.text: When they need to rest.
When they need to make a phone call.
When they want to turn around.
Never. Drivers should never drive or park on a median.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never. Drivers should never drive or park on a median.
questions.explanation: Never drive across or park on a median. It is not safe.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on your right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only if they are close by.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Don't enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a car that is close may not stop in time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the road is clear.
Come to a full stop before going forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you see these signs, you are going the wrong way and risk a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, which technique helps avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave highways as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: The faster you drive, the less grip your tires have.
Water doesn't affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road gets more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster you drive, the less grip your tires have.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less effective your tires are at removing water. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane on a layer of water.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway correctly?

options.text: Signal, let other cars pass, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly to check the traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other cars pass, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before you merge. Let other cars pass and match their speed. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers may move in the direction of the arrow if they choose.
Drivers must move in the direction of the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must stop before moving in the direction of the arrow.
Drivers must move in the direction of the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must move in the direction of the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road tells drivers they must move in that direction. Drivers must follow traffic signals before moving in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When turning left, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic pass. Always let pedestrians and other drivers already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, when exiting an expressway, when following motorcycles or bicycles, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could affect safety. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower than usual.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any safety problem must be fixed before you drive. Do not delay repairs.

questions.question: When must you always signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When entering or leaving a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps other drivers know your plans and prevents accidents.

questions.question: How do you reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Look straight ahead.
Look over your shoulder.
Look at the center of the road.
Look at the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What is the danger of driving much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It is very safe.
You always have the right-of-way.
You should block cars trying to pass.
It can create an unsafe driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can create an unsafe driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull over and let other cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks by telling people you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver wants to pass you. This gives them enough room to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. This is the only way to have enough time to respond safely.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of the above.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, your body weight, and how much time passes between drinks. Eating can slow down alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: Is it legal to leave the scene of a crash?

options.text: Yes, it is encouraged.
Yes, it is the most efficient way to handle an accident.
No, but it is acceptable.
No, it is against the law.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is against the law.
questions.explanation: It is against the law to leave a crash scene if there is property damage, injury, or death. Drivers involved must provide their information and offer help.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. You can continue, but drive at a speed where you can slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows the direction traffic must flow.

questions.question: How must a driver treat pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. You must yield to all pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When can drivers text while driving?

options.text: At red lights.
By using voice-to-text.
Never.
If they do not look at the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to text while driving a motor vehicle.
